chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abu Thabit, from Hanan, from Ibn Abi Ya'fur, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, from Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him), who said:

A mawlā (client/freedman) of ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him) died, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Look, can you find an inheritor for him?' So it was said to him (peace be upon him): 'There are two daughters in al-Yamāmah, both slaves.' So he bought them both from the wealth of the deceased mawlā, then handed over the remainder of the wealth to them both.

key_terms.مَوْلًى: Mawlā (client/freedman), a person who has entered into a patronage relationship, often with the Ahl al-Bayt.

ai.seo_question: How is the inheritance of a mawlā handled if they have no free relatives?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kāfī illustrates the practical application of inheritance law for a mawlā (client) of the Ahl al-Bayt, highlighting the Imam al-Bāqir’s (peace be upon him) method of converting slave status into heirship. By purchasing the two slave daughters from the deceased's estate, the Imam effectively freed them, thereby establishing their legal right to inherit the remainder of the wealth. This case underscores the flexibility in Shia jurisprudence regarding the status of mawali and their descendants, emphasizing the importance of lineage and emancipation in determining inheritance shares.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Abu Sabit, from hanan, from Ibn Abu Yafour, from Is’haq Bin Ammar, 
Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> has said:

‘A slave of Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> died, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Look around, can you find an inheritor for him?’ So it was said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘There are two daughters of his at Yamama, both slaves’. So he<sup>asws</sup> bought them both from the wealth of the dead slave, then handed over the rest to them both’.
en.sarwar: 8. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from abu Thabit from Hanan from ibn abu ibn abu Ya’fur from Ishaq ibn ‘Ammar who has narrated the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that a slave of Ali ibn al-Husayn, ‘Alayhim al-Salam, died. He asked to ascertain if he has left any relatives. It was said that he has two daughters in Yamamah who are owned. He (the Imam) bought them from the legacy of his slave who had died, then gave them the rest of the legacy.”’
